[Discussion] Would you rather have liked to hear Duke Nukem Forever being cancelled rather than being released?

Yes to both.

Knowing what I know now it would be better if it hadn't been released. At some point it may have gotten picked up and overhauled or redone and not sucked. They really should have just scrapped what they had and made a new game with the title rather than just updating the textures, adding cutscenes that it really didn't need, and pushing it out.

However, at the time it would have been disappointing to hear that it was cancelled. Duke 3D is amazing, and after it was announced that the sequel was finally going to see a release after years of delays it was highly anticipated.

The sad thing about it is that if it was released when it was originally being developed it would have gotten a lot of praise. It did things no other games at the time had done, the humor would have been more relevant, and the cutscenes wouldn't have been so off point. Vehicle segments and interacting with the environment the way the game does would have been a brand new thing at the time and were things that were included in the original version that ended up in development hell.

By the time it was released everything was so dated that it didn't work, and they tried too hard to make it edgy and it ended up offensive rather than working as a parody. The cutscenes would have been shorter and less gratuitous, which is why they didn't work. They went too far trying to mimic the over the top style of the original game and missed the point. Instead of clever and satirical it was just bad and juvenile.

There's a certain amount of that in Duke Nukem to begin with, but it was always satirizing the misogyny and absurdity of action heroes from the era before it was released. 4ever didn't manage to pull that off.

As the situation ended up, it was going to be a disappointment either way. If they had used the title to make something new instead of pushing out an outdated game with a texture overhaul it probably would have turned out better.
